title: Find out which package manager this Linux system uses
summary: Linux installs software with a package manager: apt, dnf, pacman or zypper. This shows which one is installed here, so you use the matching install commands.

aliases.text: what package manager do i have
how to check apt or dnf on linux
check if linux uses apt or pacman
what package manager does my distro use
linux installer apt dnf pacman zypper
apt или dnf что у меня
какой пакетный менеджер установлен в linux
какой apt или pacman у меня

prerequisites: A terminal window open on the Linux system

steps.explain: Lists the package manager programs that are installed. Normally exactly one path is printed; that manager installs software here. Nothing printed means another manager (for example apk or xbps) is used.
steps.expect: One path, e.g. /usr/bin/apt on Ubuntu, Debian or Mint; /usr/sbin/dnf on Fedora; /usr/sbin/pacman on Arch; /usr/bin/zypper on openSUSE.

steps.explain: Shows the distribution name and version. Use it together with the manager from the previous step to pick the right install commands for your system.
steps.expect: Lines such as PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS" and VERSION_ID="24.04".
